card.title: Plant Manager(Electronics Manufacturing)
card.description:
Plant Manager – Electronics Manufacturing

* **Electronics manufacturing experience**, including PCBA assembly and electronic product testing.

Key Responsibilities:

* Manage daily plant operations, including production, quality, and facilities.
* Lead production supervisors, quality teams, and maintenance personnel.
* Ensure production schedules, quality standards, and operational goals are met.
* Monitor production performance, labor efficiency, scrap, and manufacturing costs.
* Implement Lean Manufacturing, 5S, and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Oversee quality control, root cause analysis, and corrective actions.
* Support new product introductions and manufacturing process improvements.
* Maintain equipment, preventive maintenance programs, and workplace safety.
* Collaborate with engineering, planning, purchasing, and warehouse teams.
* Ensure compliance with OSHA and company safety standards.

Requirements:

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, or a related field.
* **10+ years of manufacturing experience**, including **5+ years in plant management, production management, or operations leadership**.
* Strong experience managing manufacturing teams and daily production operations.
* Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement.
* Experience with quality management, production KPIs, and cost reduction.
* Familiarity with ERP/MES systems.
* Excellent leadership, communication, and problem-solving skills.

Preferred Qualifications:

* **Electronics manufacturing experience**, including PCBA assembly and electronic product testing.
* Knowledge of IPC workmanship standards and ESD control.
* Familiarity with ISO 9001 quality standards.
* Lean Six Sigma certification.
* Experience with Epicor ERP.
* Experience managing facility maintenance and equipment projects.

Benefits

* Health Insurance
* Dental Insurance
* Vision Insurance
* Paid Time Off
* Career Growth Opportunities

card.title: Plant Manager
card.description:
**About the role:**
-------------------

As Plant Manager for Eaton’s Critical Power Solutions operations in Santa Ana, California, you’ll lead two facilities, 500+ employees, and approximately $280M in annual sales, delivering engineered-to-order critical power solutions for some of the world’s fastest-growing customers.

This is a **high-visibility business and operations leadership role** with the opportunity to make a significant impact. You’ll co-own the P&L, lead the full plant organization, and help scale the operation as demand continues to grow.

**We’re looking for a leader who can:**

* Build and develop high-performing, cross-functional teams.
* Deliver consistently against safety, quality, delivery, inventory, cost, and financial commitments.
* Create a culture of structured problem solving using A3, 8D, PDCA, and root cause analysis.
* Lead through growth, complexity, and change while maintaining strong operational discipline.
* Make sound financial decisions around cost, budgets, capital, capacity, and profitability.
* Move comfortably between the manufacturing floor, customer conversations, and senior leadership discussions.

**What you will do:**
---------------------

**Lead people and culture** 

* Build a safety-first culture where every employee owns EHS, and keep our safety management systems strong through active, visible leadership.
* Be a visible leader on every shift: communicate openly, spend real time on the floor, and build an inclusive team where people want to stay and grow.
* Model Eaton's values and Code of Ethics in how results get delivered, every day.

**Run a high-performing operation** 

* Co-own the site P&L and scorecard (safety, quality, delivery, inventory, cost, productivity and engagement), set stretch goals and close gaps quickly.
* Turn the division strategy and annual profit plan into clear short- and long-term site plans and run a disciplined daily management rhythm to deliver them.
* Lead demand, capacity and inventory planning (our Sales, Inventory and Operations Planning process) so we keep our commitments to customers and to the business.

**Put customers first** 

* Protect on-time delivery and shorten engineered-to-order and configure-to-order lead times so we win new business and grow with our customers.
* Partner with Sales, Marketing, Engineering, Project Management and Supply Chain to deliver end-to-end quality and customer satisfaction.

**Improve continuously** 

* Use the Eaton Business System and our continuous improvement tools to make lasting gains in safety, quality and productivity.
* Develop lean experts and problem-solvers on every shift, coach leaders to teach problem solving, and recognize teams that improve their own work.

**Grow the site** 

* Lead capacity expansion and footprint plans, including capital projects, new lines and cell layouts, automation and new product launches with Engineering.
* Represent Eaton in the Santa Ana community and build strong relationships with local stakeholders.

**Qualifications:**
-------------------

**Basic qualifications** 

* Bachelor's degree in business, engineering, industrial operations, or similar fields.
* Minimum 7 years of experience with progressive levels of accountability and responsibility in Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Finance, operational excellence (OPEX) and/or related support functions in a manufacturing environment.

 
**Preferred qualifications** 

* Master's in business administration (MBA) or other master's degree from an accredited institution.
* Lean and/or Six Sigma certification (Green Belt, Black Belt or Lean Tool Expert), with a track record of deploying a continuous improvement system.

• Strong understanding of Engineered to Order (ETO) and Configure to Order (CTO) business • Strong MRP / ERP platform knowledge, such as SAP or Oracle. 

* Bilingual (English and Spanish).

**Additional Information:**
---------------------------

* This role will be based at our manufacturing plant in Santa Ana, California.
* Relocation will be offered for this position.
* Eaton will not consider applicants for employment, immigration sponsorship or support for this position. This means that Eaton will not support any CPT, OPT, or STEM OPT plans, F-1 to H-1B, H-1B cap registration, O-1, E-3, TN status, I-485 job portability, etc.
* Travel required up to 25% (domestic).

All positions may require participation in video and in-person interviews as part of the hiring process. All candidates will be evaluated based on job-related competencies, and all candidates’ privacy rights and data security will be protected in accordance with applicable laws.

At Eaton, we strive to provide compensation and benefits that attract, engage, and retain the best talent. This includes competitive pay and a variety of benefit programs for eligible employees. The expected annual salary range for this role is $190000 - $278000 a year. This role is also eligible for a variable incentive program. *Please note the salary information shown above is a general guideline only. Salaries are based upon candidate skills, experience, and qualifications, as well as market and business considerations.*

We are committed to ensuring equal employment opportunities for all job applicants and employees. Employment decisions are based upon job-related reasons regardless of an applicant's race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, marital status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by law.

Eaton believes in second chance employment. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction history will be considered regardless of their arrest or conviction history, consistent with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, the California Fair Chance Act and other local laws.

You do not need to disclose your conviction history or participate in a background check until a conditional job offer is made to you. After making a conditional offer and running a background check, if Eaton is concerned about conviction that is directly related to the job, you will be given the chance to explain the circumstances surrounding the conviction, provide mitigating evidence, or challenge the accuracy of the background report.

To request a disability-related reasonable accommodation to assist you in your job search, application, or interview process, please call us at 1-800-836-6345 to discuss your specific need. Only accommodation requests will be accepted by this phone number.

We know that good benefit programs are important to employees and their families. Eaton provides various Health and Welfare benefits as well as Retirement benefits, and several programs that provide for paid and unpaid time away from work. Click here for more detail: Eaton Benefits Overview. Please note that specific programs and options available to an employee may depend on eligibility factors such as geographic location, date of hire, and the applicability of collective bargaining agreements.

card.title: Senior Manager, Production Operations
card.description:
**Be one of the Bedo 100**
--------------------------

Albedo is making Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) mainstream, building the infrastructure to enable every satellite mission to enter this new orbital domain. We build buses, integrated satellites, and turnkey missions for customers to thrive in VLEO, below 300 km, where proximity compounds performance and drag self-cleans debris.

As part of the first 100 employees at Albedo, you will have a big impact on Albedo's trajectory to proliferating VLEO — whether you're advancing hardware to increase satellite longevity, scaling production for large constellations, building next-gen flight and ground software to push performance, or enabling missions that matter for national security and our day-to-day life here on Earth.

**How We Operate:** Albedo takes a first-principles approach — in space and in business. We move with speed, take calculated risks, and learn quickly. We use AI regularly to create leverage in every discipline across the company. We work in-person at our Broomfield, CO HQ to maximize team and company productivity. We work hard and with urgency to compound our first-mover advantage.

**Who We're Looking For:** Builders who want to own outcomes, not tasks. Systems thinkers who balance precision with iteration while thinking about the big picture. Individuals who are energized by creating a category rather than competing in an existing one. You'll join a team that has already proven what others said wasn't feasible and is now scaling and upgrading our VLEO buses & payloads to serve mission sets across sensing, communications, and responsive operations.

If you can feel the excitement running through your veins, apply to be one of the Bedo 100.

### **What You'll Do:**

* Own Albedo's production operations across Supply Chain, Assembly, Integration & Test (AI&T), and Facilities, ensuring flight hardware is delivered on schedule, within budget, and to quality requirements.
* Lead and develop a multidisciplinary team of engineers, technicians, test personnel, and supply chain professionals, including hiring, performance management, and workforce planning.
* Develop and execute integrated production plans, aligning material readiness, build schedules, staffing, and test capacity across vehicle and subsystem builds.
* Set supply chain strategy and priorities, ensuring sourcing, supplier development, procurement, and long-lead planning stay ahead of production demand.
* Oversee AI&T execution from assembly through integration, functional and environmental testing, and delivery. Drive improvements in processes, tooling, and test infrastructure.
* Lead facilities and production infrastructure planning, including buildout, commissioning, equipment, capacity expansion, and EHS.
* Establish and track operational metrics, including supplier delivery, material readiness, schedule adherence, labor efficiency, throughput, and first-pass yield.
* Partner with Engineering, Quality, Program Management, and Finance to transition designs into production, resolve risks, and align resources and priorities.
* Identify and prioritize improvements to production processes, tooling, and systems, balancing cost, schedule, and scalability.
* Lead major operational initiatives, including production rate increases, facility stand-up, and ERP/MES implementations.
* Remove roadblocks, support hands-on problem-solving, and champion a culture of safety, quality, accountability, and continuous improvement.

### **Your Ideal Skills and Experience:**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Operations, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* 8–12+ years of experience in aerospace or complex hardware manufacturing, spanning production, AI&T, and supply chain, with 5+ years leading technical teams.
* Proven ability to build and manage multidisciplinary teams, including hiring, workforce planning, performance management, and employee development.
* Strong understanding of spacecraft or similarly complex hardware assembly, integration, and test, including mechanical, electrical, functional, and environmental testing.
* Working knowledge of demand planning, MRP, strategic sourcing, supplier management, and long-lead procurement.
* Experience scaling manufacturing operations and facilities, including equipment, tooling, capacity planning, and EHS.
* Ability to balance cost, schedule, quality, and technical risk while identifying constraints and driving operational improvements.
* Experience managing operational KPIs, with familiarity in ERP/MRP, MES, QMS, configuration management, and aerospace workmanship standards.
* Strong leadership and communication skills, with a hands-on, solutions-oriented approach suited to a fast-paced startup environment.

### **Salary Range:**

* $163,955 - $184,794 per year

#### **Compensation and Benefits for Full-Time Roles:**

* + Employee friendly equity compensation
 + 4% direct matching 401k
 + Health Insurance: 100% employee coverage & 75% dependent coverage
 + Parental leave and childcare coverage
 + Flexible vacation and sick time from day one
 + 12 company holidays
 + $100 monthly wellness benefit
 + Relocation package if not based in Denver

*The final compensation package is subject to change if the candidate's experience and company need drive a different job level than originally slated for the position.*

*Albedo does not accept agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to Albedo employees. Albedo is not responsible for any fees or overhead related to unsolicited resumes.*

**AI Disclosure:** We may use Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology to support and enhance our recruitment process. This includes recording, transcribing, analyzing, and evaluating your interview responses to ensure accurate, consistent, and efficient assessment of job-related skills, knowledge, and abilities. While AI tools may assist in this process, our human recruiting and hiring teams make all hiring decisions. For questions about AI use in interviews, data handling, or to request accommodations, contact Hello\_HR@albedo.com

 

**Additional Requirements:** In compliance with federal law, all persons hired must verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and complete the required employment eligibility verification form upon hire. All persons hired will be required to be a U.S. citizen, a lawful permanent resident of the U.S., or a protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

**Equal Opportunity Employer/Veterans/Disabled:** Albedo is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

**Relocation:** Relocation support for this position is available

Applicants must be a **U.S. Person** as defined under 22 CFR 120.62

#LI-Onsite

*Research shows that while men apply to jobs where they meet an average of 60% of the criteria, women and other underrepresented people tend to only apply when they meet 100% of the qualifications. At Albedo, we'd rather hear from you. We care more about how you think than which boxes you check. We value people who do the math, make their assumptions explicit, and ask the annoying questions: what breaks, what's the failure mode, what has to be true for this to work? If that sounds like you, apply, even if you don't meet every line.*

card.title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing Quality
card.description:
At GE Appliances, a Haier company, we come together to make “good things, for life.” As the fastest-growing appliance company in the U.S., we’re powered by creators, thinkers and makers who believe that anything is possible and that there’s always a better way. We believe in the power of our people and in giving them the freedom to explore, discover and build good things, together.

 

The GE Appliances philosophy, backed by three simple commitments defines the way we work, invent, create, do business, and serve our communities: *we come together*, *we always look for a better way*, and *we create possibilities*.

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire and must be able to maintain such authorization without current or future employer or school sponsorship. GE Appliances will not sponsor employment-based visas for this position now or in the future.

Interested in joining us on our journey?

 
The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Quality leads a team supporting the execution of short-term and long term projects focused on product and process quality improvement. The role supports front-line leadership and development of both salary and hourly team members in support of the factory Manufacturing Control Plans. The role is responsible for working cross-functionally to execute the overall goal for reducing the cost of poor quality associated with plant operations and product performance post-sale.

**Position**
------------

Senior Manager, Manufacturing Quality

**Location**
------------

USA, Louisville, KY

**How You'll Create Possibilities**
-----------------------------------

* Live, promote and support the Appliance Production System (APS) philosophy and drive continuous improvement in the quality and adjacent areas. Coach all team members to ensure cross-functional, focused collaboration is the way we work.
* Partner with the Quality Improvement Engineering, Business Operations and Manufacturing Engineering Leaders to promote a culture that establishes, sustains and improves product quality through engineering problem solving and discipline around supporting systems. Promote a method-based quick response to new issues.
* Responsible for developing and tracking team performance metrics tied to the overall factory (FPY, EOLA, Scrap) and effect to the product line financial plan (Damage, Scrap). Leads the team to complete projects and tasks supporting this effort. Owns and assigns tasks and establishes accountability at the appropriate level.
* Closely collaborates with the product line Engineering, Field Quality and Service organizations to understand and respond to part or system product level performance issues impacting owner use and satisfaction. Responds to this data in addition to internal data streams (leading indicators) for product quality and reliability (Engineering, EOLA and audit labs).
* Identify and execute projects to improve the cost of operations. Serve as a broad owner for Corrective and Preventative Actions (CAPA), Corrective Action Request (CAR) approach to problem solving.
* Owner of the execution of attributes of the Manufacturing Control Plan for broad areas. Responsible for the training, execution, auditing and improvement of the Manufacturing Quality Control Plan. Support efforts intended to improve workstation documentation process; create, update and maintain Manufacturing Control Instructions (MCI’s), visual aid and alerts (single point lessons) as needed.
* Strong technical aptitude and ability to coach others in complex engineering topics like dimensional control, material properties, failure analysis as well as emerging technologies such as AI
* Support analysis of data as part of Statistical Process Control (SPC) and implementation of responses as required by MCI/MCP. Escalate and measure response to data trends. Validate root cause response for effectiveness.
* Lead and support 1x1 problem solving for quality systems and related issues collaborate cross functionally to improve product quality through the identification and elimination of root cause of issues. Focus on overall repair efficiency.

**What You'll Bring to Our Team**
---------------------------------

* 8+ Years of successful experience in Manufacturing / Quality, focused on providing operational support to support operations and vertical manufacturing operations.
* Demonstrated expertise in a combination of Metrology, CMM or 3D scanning of complicated assemblies
* Ability to work within large cross-functional teams and at multiple levels in the organization.
* Demonstrated excellent communication, presentation, and facilitation skills.
* Demonstrated experience as a hands-on problem solver including complex systems (supply, build, testing and diagnosis)
* Demonstrated leadership during technically challenging and complicated cross functional projects/tasks

**Desired Characteristics**

* Engineering degree with strong content tied to understanding and impact to business financial performance
* Quality Leadership experience
* Prior experience in a union environment
* Strong organizational skills- focused on project and resource management

### **Working Conditions**

### 

* Working conditions are normal for a high-volume manufacturing environment.
* Working in this environment will occasionally require the use of safety equipment to include but not limited to: eye safety glasses, hearing protectors, work boots, and hardhats.
* These roles require frequent walking in a manufacturing plant environment.
* Travel (up to 10%) to suppliers and other manufacturing locations as needed.
* This position will be located in Louisville, KY.
* Hours & Weekends: Working off-shift and weekends may be required.

**Our Culture**
---------------

Our work is centered on our People and Culture as reflected in our Zero Distance philosophy and we recognize the importance of reaffirming our commitment to inclusion and diversity (I&D). This underscores our commitment to fostering an environment where every individual feels valued, connected, and empowered to contribute, while positioning our organization to adapt seamlessly to the evolving needs of our workforce and communities. 
 
This reflects our dedication to creating solutions that: Empower colleagues by fostering an environment where all voices are heard, valued, and encouraged to contribute. Strengthen communities where we live and work. Reinforce a culture of belonging, purpose, and engagement. Reflect the diversity of the communities we serve through our workforce, products, and practices. 
 
By further embedding Zero Distance into our People and Culture framework, we will continue to build a deeply connected organization. We are cultivating a culture of engagement, belonging, and connection, because while attracting new talent remains a priority, retention is a cornerstone of our strategy.

GE Appliances is a trust-based organization. It is important we offer our employees the flexibility they need to do their best work while balancing the needs of the business and individuals. When you join GE Appliances, you will have the opportunity to work with your leader to create a flexible work arrangement that balances the needs of the individual, team, and organization.

GE Appliances is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law.

GE Appliances participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S

card.title: Revenue - Director of Special Projects and Continuous Improvement
card.description:
**Company Description**

A best-in-class city that attracts best-in-class talent, Philadelphia is an incredible place to build a career. From our thriving arts scene and rich history to our culture of passion and grit, there are countless reasons to love living and working here. With a workforce of over 30,000 people, and more than 1,000 different job categories, the City of Philadelphia offers boundless opportunities to make an impact.

As an employer, the City of Philadelphia values inclusion, integrity, innovation, empowerment, and hard work above all else. We offer a vibrant work environment, comprehensive health care and benefits, and the experience you need to grow and excel. If you’re interested in working with a passionate team of people who care about the future of Philadelphia, start here.

***What we offer***

* **Impact** - The work you do here matters to millions.
* **Growth** - Philadelphia is growing, why not grow with it?
* **Diversity & Inclusion** - Find a career in a place where everyone belongs.
* **Benefits** - We care about your well-being.

***Agency Description***

The mission of the Department of Revenue is to collect tax and non-tax revenue due to the City and tax revenue due to the School District of Philadelphia while providing service to customers that is fair and efficient and ensuring that the City provides services that the residents can see, touch, and feel. The Department’s revenue collections enable the Administration to invest in the Mayor’s strategic priorities, including housing, education, and making Philadelphia the safest, cleanest, and greenest big city in the nation with economic opportunity for everyone.

***Work-Life***

Working hours are generally 37.5 hours per week. Our team is full-time on office days.

 **Job Description**

The Continuous Improvement Director leads the Continuous Improvement pillar within the Revenue Strategic Transformation division. This role identifies, prioritizes, and delivers process improvement initiatives that increase operational efficiency, reduce waste, and improve the experience of both employees and the residents and businesses the department serves.

The CI Director brings a disciplined improvement practice to a large public organization: mapping how work actually flows, finding where it breaks down, and redesigning it in partnership with the units that own it. Success depends on facilitation, analytical rigor, and the ability to see how decisions in one part of the department create consequences in another.

The CI Director owns the improvement methodology, process mapping and redesign discipline, customer satisfaction measurement, documentation standards, and the training that builds continuous improvement capability across the department. The role leads a small team and is expected to develop that team, not simply directing its work.

The CI Director works in close partnership with the Executive Director, who provides strategic direction, and coordinates with the division's other pillars: Operations, Project Management, Change Management, and Innovation and Advanced Analytics.

***Essential Functions***

Continuous Improvement of Methodology and Execution

* Design and maintain the department's continuous improvement framework, applying Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, root cause analysis, and process redesign methods as appropriate to each initiative.
* Lead current-state process mapping across business units, documenting workflows, identifying waste, rework, and handoff failures, and designing future-state processes in partnership with the relevant unit.
* Lead improvement initiatives from intake through implementation, ensuring changes are measurable, sustainable, and owned by the business unit responsible for execution.
* Design and maintain controls and monitoring mechanisms so improvements are sustained and do not revert to prior practice.
* Apply design thinking to identify where a local improvement would create downstream burden elsewhere, and design accordingly.

2. Intake and Prioritization

* Capture improvement opportunities from business unit requests, performance data, customer feedback, staff suggestions, and strategic priorities.
* Apply a structured prioritization framework covering feasibility screening, scoring, and portfolio balancing to select initiatives that deliver the highest value relative to effort and risk.
* Operate the shared intake and routing protocol with the Project Management Office and the Innovation and Advanced Analytics unit, so that improvement requests, project requests, and pilot concepts follow one clear path.
* Maintain a portfolio tracker providing visibility into active, pipeline, and completed initiatives with documented outcomes.

3. Customer Satisfaction Measurement

* Own design, distribution, and analysis of customer satisfaction surveys, including the external survey of residents and businesses and the internal business unit survey.
* Produce and distribute monthly reports with trend analysis and actionable insight.
* Route improvement opportunities identified through customer feedback into the intake process.
* Coordinate with Communications on distribution and messaging, and with Innovation and Advanced Analytics on data integration and reporting.

4. Standards, Procedures, and Process Documentation

* Establish departmental standards for processing documentation so procedures, workflows, and operational guides are created and maintained consistently across units.
* Provide templates, frameworks, and guidance to business units documenting their own processes, with Continuous Improvement serving as the quality standard-setter.
* Maintain a central repository of documented processes accessible to leadership and business units.

5. Training, Culture, and Team Development

* Develop and deliver a continuous improvement education plan tailored to three audiences: executive leadership for strategic awareness, managers and supervisors for application skills, and frontline staff for mindset and participation.
* Integrate a continuous improvement introduction into departmental onboarding in partnership with Human Resources.
* Identify and develop improvement champions within business units who sustain the practice beyond individual initiatives.
* Directly develop the Continuous Improvement Specialist and Project Coordinator, building their capability in process mapping, intake discipline, and initiative support.

6. Reporting and Impact Measurement

* Track and report measurable outcomes for each initiative: time saved, errors reduced, cost avoided, satisfaction improved, or other relevant metrics.
* Produce quarterly impact reports for the Executive Director documenting portfolio progress, results achieved, and lessons learned.
* Use outcome data to support the case for continued investment in staffing, tools, and initiative scope.

***Competencies, Knowledge, Skills and Abilities***

* Proven leadership in strategic planning, organizational development, and change management.
* Expertise in Lean Six Sigma, process mapping, and performance benchmarking.
* Strong ability to lead cross-functional teams and foster collaboration.
* Excellent communication, facilitation, and presentation skills.
* Advanced analytical and data-driven decision-making capabilities.

 **Qualifications**

***Required***

* Bachelor's degree in Public Administration, Business Administration, Organizational Development, Industrial Engineering, or a related field.
* Five or more years of progressively responsible experience in continuous improvement, process improvement, or operational excellence.
* Lean Six Sigma certification at Green Belt or higher, or equivalent recognized process improvement certification.
* Demonstrated command of improvement methodologies and the judgment to select the right approach for a given problem.
* Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional improvement initiatives from intake through measurable results.
* The ability to see how processes connect across an organization and how a change in one area affects others.
* Strong facilitation, analytical, and stakeholder engagement skills.
* Experience supervising, mentoring, or developing staff.

***Preferred***

* Master's degree in a related field.
* Experience in government, public sector, or nonprofit organizations.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or equivalent advanced certification.
* Change management certification such as Prosci.
* Project management certification such as PMP.
* Experience designing and analyzing customer satisfaction surveys and Net Promoter Score programs.
* Experience building an improvement function where none previously existed.

 **Additional Information**

**TO APPLY:** **Interested candidates must submit a resume.**

Salary Range: $90,500 - $115,000

**Discover the Perks of Being a City of Philadelphia Employee:**

* **Transportation**: City employees get unlimited **FREE** public transportation all year long through SEPTA’s Key Advantage program. Employees can ride on SEPTA buses, subways, trolleys, and regional rail for their daily commute and more.
* Parental Benefits: The City offers its employees 8 weeks of paid parental leave.
* We offer Comprehensive health coverage for employees and their eligible dependents.
* Our wellness program offers eligibility into the discounted medical plan
* Employees receive paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays
* Generous retirement savings options are available
* **Pay off your student loans faster** - As a qualifying employer, City of Philadelphia employees are eligible to participate in the Public Service Loan Forgiveness program. Join the ranks of hundreds of employees who have already benefited from this program and achieved student loan forgiveness.
* **Unlock Tuition Discounts and Scholarships** - The City of Philadelphia has forged partnerships with over a dozen esteemed colleges and universities in the area, ensuring that our employees have access to a wide range of tuition discounts and scholarships. Experience savings of 10% to 40% on your educational expenses, extending not only to City employees but in some cases, spouse and dependents too!

Join the City of Philadelphia team today and seize these incredible benefits designed to enhance your financial well-being and personal growth!

* ***The successful candidate must be a city of Philadelphia resident within six months of hire***

As a result, only employees in positions providing services that are patient-facing medical care (ex: Nurses, doctors, emergency medical personnel), must be fully vaccinated.

card.description:
**PLANT MANAGER**

Hussey Copper | A Pantheon Electric Company

Location: Leetsdale, PA 
Department: Operations 
Reports To: Vice President, Operations 
Employment Type: Full-Time 
Work Arrangement: On-Site 
FLSA Status: Exempt

**ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY**

Lead Operations. Drive Performance. Build the Future of Manufacturing.

At Hussey Copper, operational excellence begins with strong leadership, a commitment to safety, and a culture of continuous improvement.

We are seeking a dynamic and results-driven Plant Manager to lead operations at our Leetsdale, Pennsylvania manufacturing facility. This is a high-impact leadership opportunity for an experienced manufacturing professional who thrives in a fast-paced industrial environment and is passionate about driving performance, developing people, and delivering sustainable business results.

As Plant Manager, you will oversee the facility's manufacturing operations, including production, safety, quality, cost management, workforce development, and operational efficiency. You will work closely with senior leadership and cross-functional partners to execute operational strategies, strengthen manufacturing capabilities, and drive continuous improvement across the organization.

We are looking for more than someone who can manage production. We are looking for a leader who can inspire teams, elevate performance, and build a culture of accountability, collaboration, and operational excellence.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

Operational Leadership and Manufacturing Excellence

* Provide strategic and operational leadership for all manufacturing activities, ensuring safe, efficient, and cost-effective production operations.
* Direct daily operations across manufacturing processes, including casting, rolling, slitting, and annealing.
* Develop and execute operational plans aligned with production schedules, customer requirements, financial objectives, and business priorities.
* Establish clear performance expectations and maintain accountability for safety, quality, delivery, cost, and productivity.
* Monitor key performance indicators, including throughput, scrap, downtime, production efficiency, and resource utilization.
* Analyze operational performance and implement corrective actions to improve manufacturing effectiveness.
* Partner with Planning, Maintenance, Logistics, and other departments to optimize production schedules, equipment availability, and workflow.
* Identify and address operational challenges while maintaining a strong focus on continuous improvement and operational consistency.

Safety, Quality, and Environmental Compliance

* Champion a proactive safety culture that prioritizes employee well-being, hazard prevention, and operational accountability.
* Establish and reinforce safety standards, ensuring consistent compliance with company policies and applicable regulatory requirements.
* Partner with safety and environmental teams to identify risks, implement corrective actions, and strengthen workplace safety practices.
* Promote high standards of product quality, process reliability, and operational consistency.
* Support environmental management initiatives, including regulatory compliance, audits, annual reviews, and continuous improvement efforts.
* Ensure manufacturing practices align with organizational safety, environmental, and sustainability objectives.

People Leadership and Employee Engagement

* Lead, coach, and develop managers, supervisors, and production teams to achieve operational and organizational objectives.
* Build a high-performance culture focused on accountability, employee engagement, collaboration, and continuous learning.
* Establish clear expectations, provide ongoing coaching, conduct performance evaluations, and recognize individual and team accomplishments.
* Strengthen leadership capabilities through mentoring, performance development, and succession planning.
* Foster an inclusive and respectful work environment where employees feel valued, supported, and empowered to contribute.
* Partner with Human Resources to support workforce planning, employee relations, performance management, and organizational effectiveness.
* Maintain productive relationships with union leadership and ensure adherence to applicable collective bargaining agreements.
* Promote open communication and collaboration across all organizational levels.

Continuous Improvement and Operational Transformation

* Lead continuous improvement initiatives to strengthen productivity, operational efficiency, and manufacturing performance.
* Apply Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and structured problem-solving methodologies to eliminate waste and improve processes.
* Evaluate production workflows and operating practices to identify opportunities for increased efficiency, reduced costs, and improved quality.
* Utilize performance data and operational metrics to identify trends, address root causes, and implement sustainable improvements.
* Encourage innovation and employee participation in developing solutions to manufacturing challenges.
* Collaborate with cross-functional leaders to improve equipment effectiveness, production flow, resource utilization, and overall operational performance.
* Drive initiatives that support operational consistency, accountability, and long-term business objectives.

Financial Management and Strategic Planning

* Manage plant operating budgets, ensuring effective cost control, financial accountability, and resource optimization.
* Analyze financial and operational performance to identify opportunities for increased productivity and improved cost efficiency.
* Partner with senior leadership to develop and execute operational strategies aligned with organizational goals.
* Participate in capital expenditure planning, equipment upgrades, facility improvements, and expansion initiatives.
* Evaluate manufacturing performance and investment opportunities to support informed business decisions.
* Collaborate with Finance, Human Resources, Planning, and Logistics to align staffing, resources, and operational priorities.
* Translate business strategies into actionable manufacturing objectives with measurable performance expectations.
* Support long-term business growth and market competitiveness through disciplined operational execution.

**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business Management, Operations Management, or a related field.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in metals manufacturing.
* At least 5 years of experience in plant management or operations management leadership.
* Demonstrated success leading complex manufacturing operations and achieving measurable results.
* Strong knowledge of manufacturing processes, production management, operational efficiency, and performance improvement.
* Proven ability to lead, develop, and motivate managers, supervisors, and production employees.
* Strong understanding of Lean Manufacturing principles and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Experience managing operating budgets, interpreting financial data, and making data-driven decisions.
* Excellent leadership, communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to establish priorities, manage competing demands, and deliver results in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and comparable business applications.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Experience in copper manufacturing, metals processing, or related heavy industrial environments.
* Knowledge of casting, rolling, slitting, annealing, or similar manufacturing processes.
* Leadership experience within a unionized manufacturing environment.
* Experience implementing Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or other structured continuous improvement initiatives.
* Experience with capital projects, equipment modernization, or manufacturing process improvements.
* Strong understanding of industrial safety, environmental compliance, and quality management practices.
* Demonstrated success leading organizational change, improving employee engagement, and developing high-performing teams.

**WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE**

Success in this position requires a leader who can balance operational performance with people development, safety, and long-term strategic objectives.

The successful Plant Manager will:

* Establish a strong culture of safety, accountability, and continuous improvement.
* Deliver measurable improvements in productivity, quality, cost management, and operational efficiency.
* Develop strong supervisors and management teams capable of driving consistent performance.
* Strengthen communication and collaboration across production teams, support functions, and union leadership.
* Build an engaged and accountable workforce focused on achieving shared objectives.
* Identify and implement process improvements that support sustainable operational results.
* Align daily manufacturing execution with broader organizational goals and business priorities.

THE LEADER WE ARE LOOKING FOR

The ideal candidate is a strategic thinker and hands-on leader who understands that exceptional manufacturing performance requires both operational discipline and strong people leadership.

You are comfortable walking the production floor, coaching a supervisor, reviewing operational metrics, and collaborating with executive leadership.

You bring a solutions-oriented mindset, strong decision-making capabilities, and the ability to navigate complex operational challenges while maintaining accountability for results.

Most importantly, you understand that sustainable success comes from developing people, improving processes, and building a workplace where teams are empowered to perform at their best.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT**

This position is based on-site at our Leetsdale, Pennsylvania manufacturing facility.

The work environment includes exposure to moving mechanical equipment, varying temperatures, elevated noise levels, and active industrial operations.

The Plant Manager is expected to maintain a visible leadership presence throughout the facility while following established safety practices and operational requirements.

**ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSIBILITIES**

At Hussey Copper, environmental stewardship is a shared responsibility and an essential part of our commitment to safe, responsible, and sustainable manufacturing.

Libertas Copper, LLC, doing business as Hussey Copper, is committed to protecting the environment and promoting the safety and well-being of individuals both inside and outside the workplace. We demonstrate this commitment through environmental sustainability, responsible operational practices, and compliance with applicable local, state, and federal environmental regulations.

As Plant Manager, you will play a critical leadership role in advancing these commitments by:

* Promoting environmental awareness and accountability across all levels of plant operations.
* Ensuring manufacturing activities comply with applicable environmental regulations, company policies, and established environmental management standards.
* Participating in the Environmental Management Systems Team, including environmental policy development, annual reviews, audits, and performance monitoring.
* Supporting initiatives that reduce waste, improve resource efficiency, and minimize the environmental impact of manufacturing operations.
* Monitoring environmental performance indicators and implementing corrective actions when necessary.
* Partnering with cross-functional teams to strengthen environmental compliance, sustainability initiatives, and continuous improvement efforts.
* Reinforcing employee awareness and understanding of environmental responsibilities through effective communication, leadership, and accountability.

All employees are expected to demonstrate a commitment to environmental responsibility and actively support the company's efforts to maintain a safe, compliant, and environmentally responsible workplace.

**JOIN OUR TEAM**

At Hussey Copper, we recognize that strong operations begin with strong leaders.

As Plant Manager, you will have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact on manufacturing performance, employee development, operational efficiency, and the continued success of our organization.

If you are an accomplished manufacturing leader who is passionate about developing people, driving operational excellence, and delivering measurable results, we encourage you to apply.

Take the next step in your leadership career with Hussey Copper, a Pantheon Electric company.

**PVC Plant Manager - Dallas**

**Who we are:** 
Atkore is forging a future where our employees, customers, suppliers, shareholders, and communities are building better together – a future focused on serving the customer and powering and protecting the world.

With a global network of manufacturing and distribution facilities, Atkore is a leading provider of electrical, safety and infrastructure solutions.

 

**Who we are looking for:** 
We are currently looking for a Plant Manager to be based out of Dallas, TX. Reporting to the Vice President Operations, this person will be responsible for directing and managing plant operations for extrusion processing, maintenance, quality, and shipping/receiving. This position will coordinate plant activities through the planning with departmental managers to ensure the total manufacturing objectives are accomplished in a safe, timely and cost-effective manner.

The ideal candidate will have a Bachelor’s degree in related field and/or a minimum of 5 years plant/general management experience in a manufacturing environment or prior success as a Plant Manager or equivalent position at Atkore. Experience in lean manufacturing or business system-based company is a requirement.

**What you’ll do:**

* Provide direction, development and leadership for the facility and share best practices with other Plant Managers in running a safe, productive, cost-effective plant
* Establish and monitor overall plant performance for production and quality standards.
* Implement cost effective systems of control over capital, operating expenditures, manpower, wages and salaries.
* Participate in regular P&L reviews to ensure that budgets are met; develops and implements programs for optimal equipment utilization, equipment maintenance, and labor and material costs
* Control and minimize labor overtime, premium freight and repair expenses.
* Provide leadership and training to accomplish the company goals and objectives.
* Maintain existing plant facilities and equipment; replace or make adjustments to plant facilities and equipment when necessary.
* Manage capital asset maintenance.
* Implement and maintain preventative maintenance programs.
* Provide Safety and Health direction and support to personnel; ensures compliance with OSHA and environmental regulations.
* Incorporate shop floor organization and plant cleanliness among plant personnel.
* Demonstrate and promote our key Atkore values of Accountability Teamwork, Integrity, Respect, and Excellence, through actions and decisions.

**What you’ll bring:**

* Bachelor’s degree in related field and/or a minimum of 5 years plant/general management experience in a manufacturing environment or prior success as a Plant Manager or equivalent position at Atkore.
* Working knowledge of budgets and financial statements.
* Background with manufacturing methods, process improvement programs and procedures required.
* Advanced knowledge and experience of PVC Water pipe extrusion process preferred.
* Ability to implement Lean Manufacturing practices and drive continuous improvement.
* Six Sigma / Project Management experience.
* Excellent written and communications skills
* Computer literate. Proficiency with Microsoft Office, Excel and PowerPoint.
* Proven experience as a mentor/developmental manager for employees
* Available to occasionally work off shift to provide training and facilitate continuous improvement initiatives to all production shifts.
* Ability to work both as a member of a team, a team leader or as an individual contributor.
* Experience managing in a matrixed, mid-to-large organization
* All associates must embrace and foster and environment that supports our core values of Integrity, Respect, Excellence, Teamwork and Accountability.

 

**Within 3 months, you’ll:**

* Complete your Atkore Immersion and training requirements.
* Understand how your job will help deliver Atkore’s strategy.
* Gain an understanding of your team.
* Have developed relationships with the key stakeholders for this role.
* Be well-versed in Atkore’s Business System and the importance of your role to daily operations.

 

**Within 6 months, you’ll:**

* Maintain and be accountable for KPI visual reporting while actively participating in Lean Daily Management activities, including GEMBA walks.
* Create and modify standardized work and ensure consistent application by all team members.
* Hire talent into your organization, coach and manage performance of your team members and compensation management responsibilities for direct reports.
* Identify ways to strengthen the team’s commitment to Atkore’s core values of Accountability, Teamwork, Integrity, Respect and Excellence.

 

**Within 12 months, you’ll:**

* Be managing an efficient plant and team that delivers Atkore’s strategy.
* Have meaningful performance conversations with your direct reports.
* Be able to resolve any issues quickly and safely.

Atkore is a six-time Great Place to Work© certified company and a four-time Top Workplaces USA award winner! We’re committed to creating an engaged, aligned workforce driven by a collaborative culture. Our team **strives** for breakthrough results and **stays**focused on being standout leaders. We consistently live the Atkore mission, strategic priorities, and behaviors consistent with our core values.

**Join our team and align yourself with an industry leader!**

Placement in the range depends on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, relevant experience, skills, seniority, performance, shift, travel requirements, and business or organizational needs and may change over time. Other compensation may include, but not limited to, overtime, shift differentials, bonuses, commissions, stock, and other incentives.

Benefits available include:

* Medical, vision, and dental insurance
* Life insurance
* Short-term and long-term disability insurance
* 401k
* Paid Time Off
* Paid holidays
* Any leave required under federal, state, or local law

Benefits are subject to vesting and eligibility requirements.

Applications are being accepted on an ongoing basis.

card.description:
**Experiencing together a unique human adventure**

Animal health is key to the health of the planet. Working at Virbac means taking part in a unique human adventure in which the engagement of each individual contributes to its evolution. Encouraging internal mobility between positions and countries, offering individual development plans and building a partnership based on trust between managers and employees are as many perspectives of motivation for our teams. We also offer them a work environment conducive to exploring new territories and balancing their professional and personal lives. Finally, fostering their engagement to animal health also means listening to them and helping them to acquire new skills, preparing them for the challenges of tomorrow and encouraging them to contribute to an ever more responsible approach to our business.

**Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology**

Virbac Animal Health is seeking a Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology to join our Manufacturing Science and Technology (MSAT) team. The Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology develops, implements, maintains, and improves robust manufacturing processes and facility infrastructure for right-first-time manufacturing across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs. To plan, schedule, organize, and manage Technology Transfer Projects, CAPEX Engineering Projects, Validation, Technical Support, Alternate Raw Materials, Packaging, Life Cycle Management, and Team Leadership.

**Qualified candidates should possess the following:**

* 8 to 12+ years of Progressively responsible experience in engineering, and production management with a cGMP/FDA-regulated pharmaceutical environment.
* Demonstrated track record in CAPEX project management, facility/process design, and multi-team operational leadership across multi-site or regional organizations.
* Strong expertise in managing capital and operational expense budgets.
* Proven Leadership in process improvement , life cycle management, and technology transfers.
* In-depth knowledge of cGMP, EHS regulations, and sustainable engineering practices.
* Strong multi-team leadership, communication, and cross-functional stakeholder management abilities.

**Benefits:** 13 Company paid Holidays; 5 Floating Holidays (prorated); 15 vacation days (prorated); 5 floating holidays (prorated); 6% 401k match; competitive pay and bonus opportunity; growth opportunities within the department and much more!

**Director of NORAM Manufacturing Science and Technology**

**Area of responsibility 1: Technology Transfer Activities**

**Main activities:**

* Accountable for the budget, planning, and robust manufacturing (RFT for the first commercial batches) of technology transfer projects across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs.
* Accountable for the definition and execution of the site and regional project roadmap in alignment with business needs and capability.
* Contributes to the selection of the right technology or CMO, taking into account product needs.
* Establish robust cost estimates (CAPEX, resources, future running costs) and planning estimates to support reliable NPVs and commercial strategy.
* Leadership of scale-up batches, engineering batches, and transfer to production.
* Develops manufacturing documentation (Master Batch Records, Submission batch protocols, etc.).
* Reviews and approves transfer and submission files.

**Expected results:** Ensure the robustness and capability of the process transferred to Manufacturing

**Area of responsibility 2: CAPEX Engineering Projects**

**Main activities:**

* Support and lead CAPEX engineering projects across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs.
* Evaluate, scope, and implement CAPEX projects for facility infrastructure, process improvements, and product needs.
* Responsible for managing annual capital budgets and operating expenses for the department.
* Partner closely with key local and global stakeholders (Regulatory, R&D, Production, Quality, Supply Chain, PMO, Finance, etc.) to align project execution with regional operational goals.
* Ensure all engineering projects are performed in full compliance with applicable cGMP standards, EHS regulations, and company sustainability objectives.
* Oversee project budgets, engineering designs, contractor selection, and commissioning/qualification timelines.

**Expected Results:** Successful, on-time, and on-budget delivery of facility, process, and product CAPEX engineering projects that enhance regional capacity, EHS standards, compliance, and efficiency.

* Incorporate structured process improvement concepts (e.g., Lean, Six Sigma) across existing product portfolios.
* Lead Life Cycle Management changes to maintain and optimize the existing commercial product portfolio across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs.
* Collaborate closely with global and local stakeholders, including Regulatory, R&D, Production, Quality, Supply Chain, PMO, and Finance, to evaluate and execute LCM initiatives.

**Expected Results:** Drive continuous product and process enhancement, lower operational costs, ensure ongoing regulatory compliance, and extend product life cycles.

**Area of responsibility 4: Validation**

**Main activities:**

* Accountable for the generation, technical review, execution, and technical approval of validation deliverables (Validation Master Plan, URS, equipment qualification, process validation, cleaning validation, computer system validation)across NORAM sites and CMOs.
* Lead validation projects and teams
* Ensures risk analysis methods are applied to validation activities
* Follow industry and regulatory trends and expectations (GMP, EHS, and sustainability guidelines).
* Review SOPs and batch documentation to ensure adequacy with validation criteria.
* Ensure prompt deviation resolution, including root cause analysis when required.

**Expected results:** A thorough understanding of the validation status of the regional sites, products, and equipment, with proactive remediation plans addressing any gaps.

**Area of responsibility 5: Technical support.**

**Main activities:**

* Troubleshooting and improvement proposal of current commercial products processes (robustness, productivity, cost efficiency & compliance)
* Lean and methodological approach during trouble shooting of complex product/process deviations
* Take ownership of complex product deviation / CAPA until approval
* Contribute to solution design in collaboration with R&D, Quality Assurance, Regulatory, etc.
* Develop, apply and train teams on efficient troubleshooting and optimization methodologies (FMEA,root cause analysis, etc)

**Expected results:** Deliver strong technical and operational process mastery to support manufacturing across Virbac NORAM sites and CMOs.

**Area of responsibility 6: Alternate Raw materials**

**Main activities:**

* Technical feasibility assessments and reporting.
* Leads the engineering or validation batches (protocols/reports)
* Coordinates with the other departments (e.g. Quality Control, Regulatory Affairs)to support raw material changes.

**Expected results:** Support strategic sourcing and continuity of supply through alternate raw material qualifications.

**Area of responsibility 7: Packaging**

**Main activities:**

* Leadership of the packaging change controls and CAPAs (eg: alternate packaging components)
* Collaborates with packaging suppliers on new packaging equipment/materials, and technical feasibility assessments…
* Creates packaging specifications, including drawings and written text areas. Prepares and provides cost estimates for new packaging materials.
* Initiates, leads and Implements packaging improvements for existing products to reduce costs and/or improve packaging and product quality.

**Expected results:** Lead packaging design and modifications to drive productivity, efficiency and cost reductions while maintaining all customer and regulatory requirements.

**Area of responsibility 6: Team Leadership**

**Main Activities:**

* Translate team missions into clear, actionable SMART objectives
* Support and coach team members to help them achieve their full potential.
* Evaluate team performance through key indicators and foster a Lean culture.
* Plan and contribute to the continuous development and training of multi-disciplinary team members.
* Implement standard management practices aligned

with Virbac values while promoting a safe, sustainable working environment.

**Expected results:** Define and implement the NORAM Engineering & MSAT vision and organizational structure in alignment with group strategy.

Virbac provides numerous career opportunities, thanks to the diversity of its jobs and their international dimension.

Joining Virbac means joining dynamic teams ambitious for success.

Add Your Talent to Ours!

card.description:
**Head of Manufacturing**

**On-Site | Covina, CA | 40 hr/week**

**About Peregrine**

Peregrine Industries builds affordable, U.S.-made autonomous systems for tactical strike, counter-UAS, training, and defense modernization missions. Our platforms include Kestrel and DRACO, backed by PTEC, our modular tactical effects core.

We move fast, hold ourselves to honest engineering standards, and build hardware that has to work the first time in the field.

**About the Role**

We are seeking a hands-on **Head of Manufacturing** to take Peregrine’s production operation from 0 to 1 at our Covina, CA facility. You will stand up the systems, layout, and processes from the ground up, and own how we build quality hardware on schedule as we scale.

This is a hands-on, foundational role. You will work directly with engineering and the production team to turn prototype builds into a repeatable, quality-driven line, set the standards that hold as volume grows, and shape the manufacturing operation that delivers Peregrine’s platforms to the field. The shop floor is the face of the company, and right now it’s close to a blank canvas. How you set it up from the start is how it stays: clean, organized, and tour-ready by default.

**What you’ll do**

* Own manufacturing operations planning across in-house production, contract manufacturing, supply chain, quality coordination, and delivery readiness.
* Build and maintain capacity planning models that surface labor, material, process, vendor, and production bottlenecks before they bite us.
* Set the weekly operating cadence for production, supply chain, and shipment readiness.
* Write the SOPs, production workflows, handoff processes, and accountability structures the facility runs on.
* Establish clear KPIs for output, build cycle time, shortages, rework, supplier issues, inventory accuracy, and on-time delivery.
* Drive improvement projects that lift throughput, cut rework, and improve quality, building the repeatable processes that let us scale without last-minute heroics.
* Partner with engineering to improve assembly, integration, test, and finalization processes.
* Establish the layout, workflow zones, and standards for the Covina facility as it comes online, including designated areas for testing, harness, and soldering work, and clear homes for equipment.
* Maintain flight-ready inventory on site, with a long-term plan and projections to grow as we add hardware and people.
* Coordinate with engineering, quality, and finance so production plans are realistic and executable.
* Build the dashboards and trackers that give leadership a clear read on what’s on track, what’s blocked, and what decisions are needed.
* Help Peregrine move from low-volume builds toward repeatable, higher-volume manufacturing.

**What we’re looking for**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Business, or a related field, or equivalent hands-on experience.
* 6+ years in manufacturing operations, production management, industrial operations, hardware operations, supply chain, or a related area.
* Experience running or coordinating production in a hardware, aerospace, defense, robotics, electronics, or similar complex build environment.
* Solid grasp of capacity planning, production scheduling, inventory constraints, manufacturing workflows, and operational KPIs.
* A track record of creating SOPs, dashboards, operating cadences, and process improvements in a fast-moving shop.
* Experience working across engineering, production, supply chain, quality, and finance.
* Strong communicator who can drive accountability without leaning only on title or authority.
* Comfortable working in both strategic and hands-on modes on the same day.

**Strongly preferred**

* Experience with UAVs, aerospace, defense, robotics, electronics, or complex electro-mechanical systems.
* Experience manufacturing All Up Round weapons, munitions, energetics, or other regulated hardware under strict quality and safety controls.
* Experience with contract manufacturers, outsourced production, or supplier production readiness.
* Familiarity with ERP/MRP systems, production planning tools, inventory systems, or manufacturing dashboards.
* Experience with Lean, Six Sigma, or other continuous improvement methods.
* Time spent in a high-growth startup or a scaling hardware company.
* Familiarity with quality systems, receiving inspection, production QC, or supplier quality.

**To apply**

Send a resume to careers@pdxweapons.com

*Peregrine Industries is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status. Position is subject to U.S. export-control regulations; applicants must qualify as U.S. Persons under ITAR.*

Work Location: In person

card.description:
**Director of Quality**

**Eldridge, IA – Direct Hire**

**Full time – On Site**

Productive Resources (www.productiveresources.com) is seeking a candidate to be part of our engineering team for our customer's facility in Eldridge, IA. As a member of our team, the selected candidate will be a Director of Quality who provides strategic and hands-on leadership for quality operations and is responsible for the planning, organization, direction, coordination, compliance, and control of the Company's Quality Management System. This role leads the Quality team and ensures the effectiveness of quality processes across the organization, including product and process quality, supplier quality, inspection activities, corrective actions, audit readiness, customer quality performance, and compliance with all applicable contractual, regulatory, and government requirements.

The Director of Quality is responsible for developing and leading employees, strengthening accountability, and partnering with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Program Management, and Executive Leadership to prevent defects, drive continuous improvement, and support the safe, compliant, and on-time delivery of mission-critical products. This position oversees departmental personnel and processes, providing coaching, direction, and support to ensure the safe and efficient execution of work while maintaining quality standards, meeting customer requirements, and effectively managing operational costs. Through strong leadership and oversight, the Director of Quality ensures quality objectives are achieved and organizational performance continuously improves.

This is a full-time position that is indefinite in duration with the opportunity of professional growth, and additional opportunities within our organization.

**Duties:**

* Lead, mentor, and develop Quality managers, engineers, inspectors, supplier quality personnel, and other assigned team members.
* Establish and execute a quality strategy aligned with Company goals, customer expectations, contractual requirements, and operational priorities.
* Maintain and continually improve the Quality Management System and ensure processes remain effective, documented, implemented, and audit-ready.
* Lead internal, external, customer, registrar, and government audits; ensure findings are contained, corrected, and closed with effective corrective action.
* Own quality performance metrics and executive reporting, including product conformity, customer complaints, supplier quality, corrective action, scrap, rework, cost of poor quality, first-pass yield, and audit performance.
* Drive disciplined nonconformance control, material review, root cause analysis, corrective and preventive action, and verification of effectiveness.
